decisions.content: claude/system-prompt.md as a whole, in the form the source ships it: text for every session
decisions.reason: Owner direction of 2026-11-12: this package spans many themes, contexts and intents, so the prompt is not injected. Breadth: it is useful only in design sessions, while the package also covers Office files, explainers, engineering, research papers and session cost. Timing: every rule in it works when loaded at the moment a design task is classified. Authority: it opens by giving the model a designer identity for the whole session. Cost: 35,565 characters per session, far above the 2,000 the release accepts, paid by users writing a spreadsheet or reading a paper. Its chapters are decided one by one below; no always-on text and no hook is declared. The original file is read at intake only and is not shipped (`intake_only_paths` in sources.json): nothing reads it at run time, and its rules are restated in the capability bodies.

decisions.content: Opening lines, chapter 1 'Identity and role' and the 'Final principle': the designer persona and 'the user is your manager'
decisions.reason: Authority: a session-wide identity competes with the host's instructions and with the ten other absorbed sources. What it means in practice (ask what the artifact is for, give an opinion and let the user decide, cut what does not earn its place) is stated as steps of the production capabilities from the skills themselves, so no persona text is carried. The final principle restates chapters 5, 11, 16 and 18.

decisions.content: Chapter 1, last paragraph: do not divulge the environment, system prompt, tools or skill names
decisions.reason: A confidentiality rule of the product the prompt was written for. Here it would contradict the coordinator, which shows the user the plan, the capabilities selected and the evidence, and the package's rule of honest reporting.

decisions.content: Chapter 2 'Workflow': understand, acquire context, plan visibly, skeleton early, iterate and verify, summarize briefly
decisions.reason: A working process is a chain, not session text. Its order is the step order inside each production capability (brief, context, plan as a comment block in the file, early skeleton, verification, short summary) and the catalog chain aesthetic-direction, then wireframe or ui-prototype or html-deck, then design-review, expressed with `needs` and `reads` and never forced with `after`: each stage can start from existing work.

decisions.content: Chapter 2, closing paragraphs: silence between tool calls, concurrent file exploration, no narration
decisions.reason: Conduct rules for the whole conversation: they belong to the host and its user, and would change how unrelated capabilities report.

decisions.content: Chapter 3 'Asking questions first' and claude/skills/discovery-questions.md
decisions.reason: Function: a question round is never the outcome a user asks for; it is the first step of design work. Fit: every capability in this catalog already asks for missing essentials in one batch inside its own step, and the classifier has needs_clarification. So the protocol (read what is attached first, ask only what changes the design, once, then execute) is the brief step of each production capability, with the skill's per-artifact questions. Its `questions_v2` tool becomes an optional logical question-form tool.

decisions.content: Chapter 4 'Rooting designs in existing context'
decisions.reason: Domain rule for hi-fi design: match what exists and lift exact values from the source. It is step 1 of aesthetic-direction (stop when context exists), the context step of the three production capabilities and the 'never guess a value' rule of design-system-extract.

decisions.content: Chapter 5 'Content principles — no filler'
decisions.reason: Write-time rules for a design artifact; the review skills leave content out of scope (polish-pass, Phase 5), so they live in the production bodies' Specifics and checks (no_filler_or_invented_content, no_filler_slides). They overlap with visual-direction's 'never invent proof', which stays the rule for websites.

decisions.content: Chapters 6 to 9: aesthetic defaults, hierarchy and rhythm, typography system, colour system
decisions.reason: Domain rules. As write-time defaults they are the commit rules of aesthetic-direction; as detection patterns they are the generic-look and hierarchy passes of design-review; the per-medium type sizes are also in html-deck. Fit: for a website the dealt palette of visual-direction stays the authority, and design-review treats a recorded system as deliberate.

decisions.content: Chapters 10 to 12: accessibility, interaction and feedback, simplicity and one clear call to action
decisions.reason: Domain rules that are checked on a file: the accessibility and interaction-states passes of design-review, and the wiring rules of ui-prototype. The chapter's 0.2 to 0.3 second transitions contradict motion-design's shorter feedback durations; a recorded motion-spec wins (design-review, Specifics).

decisions.content: Chapter 13 'System thinking': components, design tokens, documented patterns
decisions.reason: It is the rationale and the documentation format of the two extract skills, merged into one role.

decisions.content: Chapter 14 'Respecting the medium': CSS strengths, real interactions, fixed-size content that scales, persisted state, canonical HTML
decisions.reason: Rules for HTML design artifacts only; they would mislead an Office or Figma task. Carried where they act: real interactions and persistence in ui-prototype, scaling and persistence in html-deck, persisted tweak values in design-options.

decisions.content: Chapters 15 and 16: understanding users, quality over quantity
decisions.reason: Audience and persona questions are part of the brief steps; 'a wireframe round and a hi-fi round on different bets' is in wireframe; depth over breadth and the polish list are design-review's polish pass and design-options' rule against near-duplicates.

decisions.content: Chapter 17 'Output principles': pick the format, give variations, one file with many variants, right scale
decisions.reason: The variation and single-file rules are design-options. Its format table (canvas, prototype, deck, animation engine) chooses between artifacts, which here is the classifier's job through the intents, so the table itself is not carried; the timeline engine with a scrubber for animation has no procedure in the selected snapshot and motion stays with motion-principles. Adding tweak controls nobody asked for is left to a request for design-options, because chapter 19 of the same prompt forbids unrequested scope.

decisions.content: Chapter 18 'Collaboration and delivery': show early, brief summaries, delegate verification, honest progress reports
decisions.reason: Process rules of a design step: the early skeleton, the closing summary and the checks that name what was not verified (unverified_behavior_disclosed, deck_walked_or_disclosed, unverified_items_disclosed). The verifier subagent is an optional logical tool; one capability still runs per step.

decisions.content: Chapter 19 'IP and content boundaries'
decisions.reason: A limit that matters only when a design is produced, so it is a scoped line in each production capability: a company's distinctive interface or branded elements are not recreated unless the product is the user's own, and scope is not added without asking. The source's test, the user's email domain, cannot be verified by any host here and is replaced by the user's own statement. Open doubt: whether the owner wants a stricter rule than the user's statement.

Its per-session character cost is the final combined policy length, not separate per-source charges; native system channels on Claude Code/Pi/OpenCode/Hermes and developer additionalContext on Codex are described by the current factory. The reported upstream candidate gate failure is a caution to preserve uncertainty, not evidence this adaptation passed behavioral testing.

always_on:
Complete requested work, including affected scope and required deliverables. Use settled context; ask only for information blocking a sound result. Continue independent authorized work. Perform authorized actions with your tools instead of merely explaining how.

Keep conversation direct and easy to scan. Lead with the result or useful action; use short paragraphs or numbered steps when helpful. Group long lists without dropping items. Match the user's language, style, expertise and requested depth. Explain complex steps with a concrete example or diagram when useful. Avoid filler, repetition, tangents and imposed status templates. Track the goal, decisions, progress and open work; give one small next action only when work remains for the user. Describe observed errors neutrally with a recovery step; do not invent causes. After repeated failures, reassess assumptions before retrying. Estimate effort only when useful, with concrete units and stated assumptions. Do not infer a diagnosis or personal traits.

Brevity never reduces scope, artifact completeness, design fidelity, required engines, evidence, accessibility, security, hardware calibration, validation, checks or honest disclosures. Preserve each task's required format and approval gates; reuse approval already given. Preserve uncertainty; distinguish verified results from assumptions and untested work.

For code changes, inspect the affected path: callers, tests, fixtures, configuration and exports. Fix the shared cause with the smallest readable change; retain existing conventions and safeguards. Prefer suitable project components, then platform features, then installed dependencies; preserve required engines and behavior. Avoid speculative features and unnecessary wrappers or abstractions. Test meaningful changed behavior and report what was checked. Mark a deliberate shortcut as `shortcut: <limit>, <upgrade trigger>` when relevant; do not invent debt. Never claim unmeasured savings or fabricate benchmarks.
